samples.identity: Warlock/Longlegs-style deployment and remote-access batch script
evidence: 321-byte unobfuscated batch: quiet remote MSI installation; VS Code tunnel service registration from Windows/debug; SYSVOL wildcard copy into Public and background cmd launch with stderr discarded.
Symantec reports the exact MSI URL and debug-directory tunnel command, plus the matching SYSVOL/Public copy-launch mechanism. Domain and payload names here differ from the published redacted example.

No ransomware encryption or credential theft implementation is present in this script. Suspicious findings express the evidenced deployment/access combinations, rather than claiming the unseen payload behavior.
changes: Remote msiexec URL is notable capability; suspicious C2 combinations now require the debug-directory tunnel registration.
SYSVOL/Public copy-launch moved from GPO lateral movement to micro-behaviors/process/deploy; matcher preserved, description states proximity rather than bound data flow.
Removed redundant copy+Public-path staging composite and Public-path alternative from generic evasion composite. Underlying copy, path and launch observations remain.

evidence: Manifest and source implement the documented OpenCode agent-orchestration plugin.
win32.test.ts passes encoded command strings to detectPowerShellEscape and checks booleans. The detector uses regex tests, not shell execution.
Both UTF-16LE Base64 strings decode to IEX (New-Object Ondows Nem); this malformed command is inert escape-detector test input.
samples.residual: One unique suspicious ID, binary/embedded/base64-powershell, repeated on container, member and decoded layers. This is engine-generated, cannot be overridden by YAML, and is not evidence of test-input execution.
